titleStmt.title: Selections from "My Awe #8: The Winter Desperation Issue"
titleStmt.author: >Verna Doherty
Randy Strickfaden
Bruce Storm

publicationStmt.p: This publication is part of the assigned work for the University of Washington class "Texts, Publics, and Publication." Our team chose to digitize selections of "My Awe #8" for people like ourselves: who are interested in zines as counterculture and as representations of artistic and political movements, and who are interested in the form as a collaborative artistic endeavor free of the expectations of traditional publication. We feel that this particular zine represents an interesting moment in Seattle’s political and art history. We chose selections that we believe highlight the patchwork nature of the zine, spotlighting pieces of prose, poetry, political commentary, illustrations, and the front matter, for what they all reveal about the ethos behind the zine’s publication.

sourceDesc.p: The zine is made up of a combination of illustrations, handwriting, and type. The font of the type seems to be a Courier font of some kind. The handwriting is usually in all-caps and generally legible, sometimes written in spirals around the illustrations or the typed text on each page. The selections we have chosen are a representative sample of the types of text included within the zine, including some illustrations, pages with typed text, and pages with handwritten text.

normalization.p: In our edition, we maintain the distinction between type and handwriting, the incorporation of visual elements into text pages, and typographic features (including errors), which are part of the low-polish appeal of this art form. We annotate the difference between type and handwriting, as well as the pattern the typewriting takes; political context such as local and national government; information about relevant music or art, as best we are able to find it; and what author information we can find. In order to stay faithful to the ephemeral nature of zines, we have decided not to include images in this transcription; we will include the location of where images occur and a description of what they are, but not the image itself.

correction.p: We have maintained typewriter errors and misspellings where we found them, but have annotated such errors. We did not maintain line breaks in prose, so anytime that there is a word sepreated by a hyphen, we replaced with the full word; this is marked with tag.

segmentation.p: Our edition excerpts four items from this Zine:

bibl.author: Verna D.
bibl.title: "Denny's Was Closed, A Saga in Portland"

profileDesc.creation: This zine represents much of the rhetoric and aesthetics of what would be known as the Grunge movement, which has its origins traced to Seattle in the 1980s. References are made to punk and grunge bands, musicians, and locations of the era. The political commentary of the zine often either directly or indirectly addresses the reader with the intent of expressing frustration or warning about the governments and institutions the zine is pushing back against.

div.p: So, you want uh job here do ya, security and steady pay, and mabe even uh chance to move up, well then peon piss in this cup! And if your urine's clean then we just might hire you, and use ya 'till the job is through. We'll work you like uh whore until we don't need ya anymore; then, we'll dump ya back with all the rest of the applicant junkies who failed our tinkle test.

Yep, they got it in for all the dopers now, and there's all kinds of brand new witch-hunts. With here, their scapegoat reason is having to do with job performance. Where over the weekend, huh! in your free time, you break the law by smokin' your J with the drapes pulled shut to keep from gettin' busted, and show up for work next Monday mornin' refreshed, well rested, and attitude adjusted. While your law-abiding co-worker shows up with an aching head, swollen face, incoherent still with every crooked step uh stagger, trip, and toddle after spending their whole weekend nippin' from uh bottle.

p.hi: will come down on civil-liberties and civil-rights

div.p: Yet, the test results show that your the one that has to go. Your drug of choice is not approved by law ya know. And it renders you unfit for work, while that other drunken jerk, with his bloodshot eyes and big red snout, passes the test with flying colors no matter how much stale booze he excretes out.

Oh yes, and with this drug, sniff sniff, there can be no casual use. Once you've done it your hooked for good and destined to uh life of abuse. And Uncle Same has waged his war patrolling every border and every shore, moving his troops through every town to combat the home grown dope, crack, and heroin brown. You know, you hear about it all on the news. Ironic as hell now they tolerate cigarettes and booze. In fact, your tax dollars have even helped subsidize that little enterprize.

If people choose to be dumb instead of think by wasting their livers with too much drink then I say leave um alone and let um go. Let um fry their lungs smokin' tobacco. Let um get stones to the bone and relieve their stress; give um the freedom of choice to make their lives uh mess. Let um eat all the psychedelics they want and blow their minds even worse, so they may attain an even grander misinterpretation of the universe. Let um rot their nerves by firin' smack,
and pack their noses 'till they all have uh heart attack.

Because, to some extent people will always use this stuff, so why waste more of out money in gettin' tough. I suppose to impress the redneck voters and cash in on some power and glory. Now if someone shows up for work buzzed out of their head, well I agree, that's uh different story. But they shouldn't be persecuted for what they used on their day off whatever its kind, and is now in their bodily waste and no longer in any way affecting their state of mind.

And it has recently been suggested that all dope peddlers who get arrested if found guilty should be sentenced to death thinking this way that they all shall soon breathe their last breath. Well yee ha! let's whip out thee ol' hangin' rope for everyone caught sellin' dope. And even though it doesn't serve to really deter crime, it will still satisfy the citizen for the time; the innocent victims demanding justice through more gore. Gas um, fry um, hang um, shoot um, give um what they hunger for.

Oh yes, we sure got ourselves something worse than big brother, much more old schooled, fashioned, and primal in thought it is none other than not one but a whole coalition of big bad grandads. Who with regard to the issue of civil liberty are creating quite an upheaval as they crack their whip attempting to impose their censorship so we don't see and speak and hear no evil. And by them doing this, these demagogies, these greedy hogs, these savage dogs with the flesh of Latin America hanging from their carnivorous tooth, they conveniently close down the peaceful venues of their opposition used by those who care and speak the truth.

p.hi: Scalia has consistenly expressed narrow view of the First Amendment.

div.p: And they want to get all the smut and naked bare fannies away from the children, and the God-fearin' great grannies. In fact they say, that nowhere at all should this stuff be within a trule wholesome society. They wanna get all the dirt of the t.v., radio, records, and yes, even home video tape. After all, the theologian general has now determined that the 1st amendment causes people to murder and rape. And as well I say, from the standard norm not too far should you rome, 'cause these autocratic snotties are even tryin' to tell consenting adults what they can and can't do with their own bodies in the privacy of their home. They go for yer standard missionary position between man and wife shackled by god & state 'till death do them part. This is the secual interplay which they grant as being OK. As for any other, well, the morally almighty have rated X, so as to stop for good any other form of innovative sex.

Yea, they're passing new laws everyday, and there's little we can do. Laws which by their design serve to intrude upon and entrap you. But I guess we shouldn't worry, because, any major cases, according to due process, they will formally list um, and they may be brought before the newly remodeled, narrow-minded, ultraconservative, religion bound, supreme court legal justice system.

p.hi: The powerful anchor of the court's right wing

div.p: I myself am really worried about our lady lib. I don't want to see her boasted pride transformed into uh fib. And even though her outside they have recently seen fit to overhaul, the ol' gal on the inside might not be standing quite as tall. Her true symbolism seems to be fading, and who knows, may even soon be gone. And then alls we've got us is just another paradoxical icon.

And on the subject of terrorism, out brilliant leaders, who are the ones that I say belong in jail, counteract by committing it themselves, but only on a bigger scale. And they claim this is done in self-defense, and so as to give the U.S. the upper hand; committing the same crime as them saying it's the only language they understand. They bomb the innocent people of some country whos tyrant leader doesn't seem to in the water have both of his oars, and who also, just our own, sponsors bullshit wars. Out of the bellies of their jets they let the bombs fall upon civilian folk who are as well burdened with great social ills that are potentially common to us all. They bomb um while they barter in the street, and how the ground beneath their bare feet. They bomb a nation of people whos beliefs, culture, and value of life is far different than our own. A group, who to keep from adding fuel to an already burning fire we should of course protect ourselves from, but then best leave alone. They bomb this group of people whom for so long have not had the chance to live conceptually, nor any other way free, for hundreds of years governed by coercive rule which has served to form their warped mentality. And it's just this sort of thing that's got me so uptight, for concern that in becoming this way too my own country just might. Our leaders bomb and bomb yet against this wave of terrorism they fail to stop, slow down, curtail, or even barely nudge it. I think it's all just another way they can try to justify their outrageous defense budget.

div.p:
And they, who claimed to be so concerned about balancing the budget, and the out of control government spending. Well, judging from their own hypocritical record of the sincerity of their concern I think they should have uh hard time defending. Yet, the voting public who took their bate have still seen their deficit grow, but only at uh
faster rate. And further I note, the publics' revenue they have stole away from me and you, and used it for their own pet projects which, believe me, don't do us any good, and have ignored their true responsibility of office, whereas, otherwise it MIGHT have been used as it should.

When it comes to representing the people, I ask: is this present leadership our best choice? Does it really represent the peoples' voice? With these now who hold the power are we better set? or are those who call the "do-gooders" the lesser of two evils, and really our best bet? Those who will respect a person's right to be free, and live uh life of quality. Those who will when they preach truly teach the significance of both liberty and equality. And concerning these two topics, will not only expound of them in their speech, but really work hard also in the name of each. Those who with out precious environment will protect from further damage, and be ethical at using their know-how to responsibly manage. Those who will adequately defend the nation's ground while will still work to make relations between us and other countys not as tense, and who to their defense contractor buddies wont be throwing the money all around at the taxpayers' expense. Those who will not lie, but instead address the true issues of out time; the ones of the most relevance. Those who are, oh yea sure full of love, peace, and vision, but much more so than that capability and intelligence. Those who use diplomacy, negotiation, and cooperation as their tools when amongst ourselves or with others we get into uh fix, and will do their damnedest to keep us out of any violent conflicts. Those who with out world neighbors--the citizens of other states--will not intervene in what is really their affair for not the slightest length of duration, and will instead respect these peoples' sovereign right to self-determination. Those who through some half-assed mediocre way will at least use our money in an attempt to do good deeds by supporting programs for society; things that everybody needs. Instead of for some nuclear reactor where we the people are in no way the real benefactor, or for increasing the chances of annihilation everywhere so that everything may soon be gone, they will funnel the bucks toward desperately needed education, healthcare, and so on.

figure.figDesc: The image lies in the left margin of the page and spands about 15 lines of text. It depicts the side profile of Reagan wearing a suit and tie

div.p:
Yep, if we're ever fortunate enough to once again get those "do-gooders" back, of course we should feel beter for the time while our itch is gettin' scratched, but we shouldn't feel so damned good that we start countin' out chickens before they are actually hatched. For
then will not be the time to forget, relax, and concern ourselves once again with only havin' fun, for then will be the time to get some change for the better kind of work once and for all done. Perhaps we can revise the system in a way which will make out democracy more foolproof, and will serve to eliminate the financial support from greedy slobs backing any ol' incompetent goof. I say create a political process which is bound by a code of ethics, and discipline to be enforced by a constitutional mandate. And for the purpose of insuring capability, set intellectual prerequisites for every candidate. Let's revise out democracy in a way where we all can be glad. Once changed for the better so as to protect us from any big brother whom would run for office wishing to do bad.

But for now it looks like we're stuck with this one, and it offers us few preventions that those with bad intentions will not ascent to the seats of power so that in them we the people have sit "creeping Orwellions" who for me and you care not one single bit, and are themselves for this job not at all fit.

And what's the result for all of us? What is our reward? Well let's celebrate, time to pour the champagne, just like the president promised throughout his campaign we get ta see um bring America back, but never move 'er forward.

div.note: In deciding what to publicize and whether to publicize it, we are aware of the tendency of more formal publishing to co-opt underground (and often very personal) cultural objects such as zines, bringing them into mainstream culture and thereby both robbing them of their subversive power and exposing those who participate in these movements. Ann Japenga writes about the mainstream co-optation of Riot Grrl culture, arguing that “An authentic counterculture is as necessary to the larger society as the rain forest is to the planet. It's a protected laboratory where evolution can take place.” She writes about Riot Grrls crying over the exposure of their privacy and the secrets they shared in their zines. Although several decades have passed since this zine was created, and it is now closer to a historical artifact than an immediate revelation, we try to maintain this ethos in our editorial choices. For this reason, we have chosen to censor personally identifying information such as phone numbers. (However, we have retained addresses that lead to PO boxes, as we imagine those are not directly associated with specific people.)

"Creeping Orwellianism" is a political prose piece/rant about invasive drug testing policies. It is likely a reference to the Anti-Drug Abuse Act of 1986, which was "the Reagan Administration’s response to a national moral panic around crack cocaine" and drastically increased criminalization of drugs, which has contributed to mass incarceration (Lipke)

"Ol Gory" is a politically charged poem criticizing what was then the current state of US militarism and nationalism. The name "Ol Gory" is a play on words for the term "Old Glory," as in the flag of the United States. The imagery portrays the staining of the flag through the wrongdoings of the American Government. In many radical eyes at the time, America was no longer the leader of the "free world," but rather a "fanatically capitalist power, willing to follow militarist policies of nuclear intimidation and conventional military intervention to protect its politico-economic interests".

In the case of typewritten or handwritten text in which one letter was typed or written on top of the previous, however, we have read the word as we assumed it was meant to be written for simplicity's sake.

In the physical layout of "Denny's Was Closed, A Saga in Portland," each page is mostly typed, but includes handwritten prose in spirals around the page.re To represent this in TEI, we have placed all the handwritten text together in a section at the beginning of the entry with page breaks entered into it to indicate which page it surrounds.
"Lude" here is likely referring to a pill of methaqualone, a sedative. The term is short for Quaalude, a brand name for methaqualone.

William Hubbs Rehnquist was an Associate Justice from 1972 to 1986 and the Cheif Justice from 1986 to 2005. He was known for his conservative positions opposing, abortion rights and anti-discrimination laws; however, he also showed he could compromise when he "wrote the majority opinion upholding Congress's right to appoint independent counsels to investigate and prosecute high government officials, a right that was challenged by the Reagan administration."

Flipper is a band formed in 1979 which endured several on-again off-again breakups over the next few decades, and which specializes in “haunting drone rock” and “philosophizes about boredom” as part of punk’s general expression of dissatisfaction with the status quo (Goldberg).

"The Yobs" is likely the reversed name for the band "The Boys," an English punk rock band formed in 1976. Every Christmas, the band reversed their name to read "The Yobs" and released an album under that name (Wikipedia).

“This landmark Northwest 23rd Avenue coffee shop was open 24 hours a day, making it a haven for 1980s punk rockers and club kids, who would flock here after bars closed for pre-dawn scrambled eggs. Before Oregon’s indoor smoking ban, this was a restaurant that eagerly welcomed smokers, and it seemed like everyone at the counter took drags of cigarettes between sips of strong coffee. “QP,” as it was called by regulars, closed in 1992 after 58 years of great people-watching.” (Umbrella Project)
